#1329. The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'

Spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

#1328. Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer said he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain said.

"I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure." Captain Bruno Fernandes gives his immediate reaction to Manchester United's heavy 4-1 defeat to Como 🗣️ 🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/8bzmLGkRAX

Carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

United enjoy a spell inside the attacking third to close the half, but it’s too late, at least for the first 45 minutes. The referee blows his whistle and we reach half-time with Como a goal to the good.

There are boos at half-time from United’s travelling support.

United send both of their full-backs forward and it gives Cunha the space to get a shot away from just outside of the box, but his curled effort sails over.

There will be one minute of time added on at the end of this half.

That’s a let off for United. Yan Couto, one of two former Manchester City signings in the Como team, carves open the United defence with a lovely pass and Douvikas should have done better with the finish.

Amazing the difference when you have a centre forward prepared to run in behind. Who would have thought it?

Baturina is the latest to threaten Lammens’ goal. His strike from the edge of the box stings the Belgian’s gloves and Douvikas, who attempts to latch on to the rebound, is offside.

Penalty shout for Como! Douvikas is sent through and it looks as though Lammens is in trouble as he sticks out a leg over which the Greek tumbles, but replays show Lammens withdraws his outstretched limb in the nick of time.

There was also an offside in the build-up, so it does not matter anyway.

Milla and Perrone are really pulling the strings in Como’s midfield. The former comes from the Jose Bordalas/Getafe school of football (think Tony Pulis during peak Britannia era) but you would not guess it given the way he manipulates the ball.

This game has entered into something of a holding pattern, with Como retaining possession as United chase shadows, desperately trying to lock off the centre of the park.

Here, Coute inverts, picking up the ball in the inside right channels before spinning in a ball over the top for Douvikas to stride on to, but the Greece forward shanks his shot over the bar.

Thirty four minutes in and the first chants of “attack, attack, attack” can be heard from the United fans. There is currently a giant hole where you would expect United’s strikers to be. It’s so poor.

Lammens does well to get down smartly and keep out a Douvikas effort, speared towards the near post after a sweeping counter attack. The resulting corner fails to threaten United’s defensive unit.

Da Cunha, fresh off his first France call-up, has just sold Mazraoui a dream, spinning the Moroccan in the middle of the pitch before gliding upfield, sweeping the ball out to Valle on the left, whose cross is far too loopy to trouble Lammens.

For seemingly the first time in this match, one of United’s full-backs, Mazraoui, makes a darting run in behind. While the ball goes through to the goalkeeper, it’s the right sort of intent.

Paz escapes the vicious clutches of Santos, but bumps into Cunha’s outstretched leg and earns a foul near the halfway line. Santos, already on a yellow, will need to careful not to get caught doing anything untoward for the remaining 60 minutes of this match.

It’s hard to detect a game plan from United. Como look like they know what what they’ve been told to do but United are just all over the place. Andrey Santos will be grateful referee Sven Jablonski was lenient the first time he came through the back of Paz because he’s just scythed through him a second time minutes later and picked up a yellow.

That’s better from United. Cunha hits the by-line aggressively but his cross is cut out.

Paz then breaks away down the right and, sensing a lack of cover, Santos dives in and receives a yellow card for his troubles.

United string together perhaps their best sequence of the match, shifting the ball quickly from one side to the other, with Mount and Cunha combining, but the move breaks down when Tielemans’ attempted through-ball is cut out by Kempf.

Fernandes attempts to play in Tielemans between the lines but his pass is behind the Belgian and Como regain possession. It’s rinse and repeat moments later, but on the far side.

The detail on United’s passes has been so poor thus far, with Como picking up loose balls all over the pitch.

Penalty shout for Como! Da Cunha, Douvikas and Baturina combine expertly through the middle, trading the ball with cultured one-touch passes. Baturina is felled by Maguire inside United’s box just as he was gearing up to shoot, but neither the referee nor the VAR are minded to intervene. There is a touch, but it does seem very slight.

United have gone with the box midfield once more, with Fernandes rolling inside as a false 9. Como are counteracting United’s movements through Paz dropping in, so Carrick’s men are struggling to take control of the central zones.

Mbeumo bursts towards the by-line but Ramon gets back sharply to divert the ball behind for a corner, which is easily dealt with.

United drop into a deep block, forcing Como to build around the outside. The ball is worked to the adventurous Couto who loses his boot after an overzealous challenge from Cunha and he earns a free-kick for his troubles, but Da Cunha’s delivery fails to beat the first man.

Chance! Da Cunha plays a lovely through-ball into the right channel for Paz to gallop on to and he flashes the ball across the face of goal, but Maguire gets there before Douvikas and the ball is cleared.

United are struggling to string passes together as Paz cuts out a Lammens pass out from the back, but he cannot keep the ball in play.

United need to settle, and here they decide it best to keep hold of the ball for a while. There are a few sideways passes but the ball goes back to Como.

Valle makes a burst down the left and Dalot’s contact results in a foul, but the free-kick is not up to much.

Como 1 Manchester United 0 (Paz) Well, we said he was special! Como work the ball out to the right, with Da Cunha picking out Paz on the edge of the box. Neither of United’s centre-halves are minded to close the Argentine down, and he opens up his body before shaping the ball around Lammens and inside the far post. Golazo.

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick said before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

“But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.”

Como finished last season with a stadium that did not meet Uefa’s Champions League ground requirements, so work began immediately to ensure it would be ready for the 2026-27 season.

This included the construction of a new stand, where the old “Curva Como” once stood, which would increase the stadium’s capacity to 12,379, as well as a pitch expansion, instalment of undersoil heating and upgraded media and hospitality sections.

Andrey Santos, one of United’s summer signings, was asked for his thoughts on Lisandro Martínez’s explosive interview in which he took aim at the club’s hierarchy for their strategy in the latest transfer window. The Brazilian said: “We know the comments [of] Licha, but I think now it’s done so we have to move on and focus on tomorrow [Wednesday].

When pressed on whether Martínez had addressed the squad about his remarks, Santos added: “No, no, no. Nothing happened, as you know we are on the same page, so we believe in ourselves, in your team-mates, your coach, your staff, so I think this is the most important.”

It’s happened before where players have played in the Youth League then made the senior bench later in the day although the very youthful bench is a reflection of just how many absentees Carrick has at the moment.

Cesc Fabregas has done a fine job at Como and will hope to further enhance that burgeoning reputation with an historic win. United desperately need results - it’s two wins in 10 in all competitions - and face Bournemouth on Sunday after this.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Absolutely tipping it down in Como, with 64mm of rain forecast before #MUFC kick-off here tomorrow ☔️ https://t.co/WvI3X8dilh

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

#1326. Sarri: ‘Atalanta strength of character, but hire someone else for man-marking’

Maurizio Sarri hails Atalanta’s ‘character’ to fight back from 4-2 down for a 4-4 draw with Inter, but warns he will not abandon his tactical ideas. ‘If they want man-marking, then hire someone else.’

La Dea have the unexpected honour of playing in both 4-4 Serie A thrillers this season, as they were held here by the same result against Frosinone on October 25.

They refused to give up, even when trailing 4-2 to a Pio Esposito hat-trick and Petar Sucic penalty, because Eljif Elmas, a Charles De Ketelaere double and stoppage-time Franck Kessie spot-kick allowed them to snatch a point from reigning Champions of Italy Inter.

“This team is starting to have some strengths, and the first is its character, because this is not the first time that the team has fought back, while we are also scoring more goals recently,” Sarri told DAZN Italia.

“Unfortunately, we also still have a big weakness, which is the defensive fragility that sees us concede far too many. I am seeing progress, though.”

Atalanta remain in 12th place in the Serie A table, with just one win in their last six league games, but in the circumstances this point can be a valuable confidence-booster.

They conceded 24 goals, the seventh worst defensive record in the top flight, and only scored 21.

“We had a lot of injuries, that never allowed us to start the same set of defenders. There is also a packed fixture list, so we do not have time in training to work on the defensive movements,” noted Sarri.

“We must not forget this was a squad accustomed to defending in a completely different way. I don’t see it as just one problem, but rather a collection of circumstances that are making things difficult for us.”

Gian Piero Gasperini set the template in Bergamo for so many years with his three-man defence, so changing to Sarri’s four at the back and zonal marking is proving a very difficult transition.

“If Atalanta want someone who tells their defenders to man-mark, then they need to hire someone else,” smiled the coach.

“I have never done that and I have absolutely no intention of doing it in future, in all honesty.”

De Ketelaere was named Man of the Match by the Lega Serie A, despite Pio Esposito scoring a hat-trick, as he bagged two goals and earned the penalty.

“His last few performances for us have been good, and he carried that on when playing for Belgium. Charles has been on form for over a month now, he’s strong physically, talented technically, has immense potential. He has these ups and downs, which he has had throughout his career, and we are working on smoothing those out.

“I’ve coached some talent in my time, but few with his potential.”

Atalanta have a famously poor record against Inter, scraping seven draws and 11 defeats since the 4-1 victory here in November 2018.

#1324. Premier League x Stonewall partnership ends, new LGBTQ+ campaign to be launched

The Premier League is set to introduce a new LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

Stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, launched in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences."

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent issue.

Controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped plans for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players currently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs new campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

#1321. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 06:50 EST, 22 November 2026

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

#1320. Chivu: ‘Inter failed the exam, too soft and shallow’ in wild 4-4 with Atalanta

Cristian Chivu warns Inter ‘failed the exam’ in their 4-4 draw with Atalanta, criticising some of his players. ‘We were too soft, need to be more determined in the duels.’

The Nerazzurri performed several remarkable comebacks this season, but they were on the wrong end of it tonight in Bergamo after fumbling a two-goal advantage three times.

Pio Esposito scored his first ever Serie A hat-trick, carrying on the remarkable form seen for Italy in the Nations League, and the Petar Sucic penalty had seemingly put the game to bed at 4-2.

However, Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the game and a Franck spot-kick in stoppages allowed Atalanta to claw their way back for 4-4.

“We were leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, so this is the regret,” Chivu told DAZN Italia.

“We had an idea of what we should’ve done and did not do, we should’ve controlled the advantage, then when we felt them snapping at our heels, we immediately restored the two-goal cushion.

“I think we failed the exam in the final minutes. It’s hard to say why we were unable to control the lead. We have to congratulate Atalanta, as they sensed that we were a bit shallow, and pumped crosses into the box, put bodies in there, while we were a little soft compared to our usual approach.

“I’m sorry, I see this as two gifted points, but we will learn from it and know now to let the intensity and mentality drop in the next games.”

Inter were angry at the Davide Zappacosta penalty for clearing off the line with his elbow because it was only a yellow card and not a red.

Alessandro Bastoni also felt the decisive spot-kick was harsh, but while his handball was unintentional, the arms were raised above his shoulder and therefore in a punishable position.

“The second Atalanta goal came from a corner, identical to one where Pepo had just made a great save moments earlier, so we did not learn from it,” continued Chivu.

“When we got to 4-2, our defence was then static in a chaotic situation. We need a certain determination and focus in these situations, and we were negligent in that area today.”

There was another serious blow today along with the dropped points, because Hakan Calhanoglu limped off with a suspected flexor strain in the first half.

At least Curtis Jones and Lautaro Martinez made their comebacks after more than a month out, two in the case of the former Liverpool midfielder.

“I felt we were suffering on the wings, partly because we were too soft, we were allowing the space to put the crosses in too easily. I decided to put Marcus Thuram wide to help out Djed Spence in the final stages,” explained Chivu.

“It’s a matter of desire to go into the duels, to be more determined, not just put bodies behind the ball, because if you don’t have the right intensity then a single error can be costly.”

Inter have conceded 17 goals in 12 Serie A games, more than any other side in the top six, but this is their first draw of the entire season after 11 wins and three defeats in all competition.

Is Chivu more angry at the dropped points, or worried at how many goals Inter are conceding this season?

“We are conceding too many goals for a club that has high ambitions, but we must do like we did in Rotterdam and with Como, respond to a setback, not look over our shoulders to the past. We must learn that we cannot just control a situation, we’ve got to keep giving 100 per cent until the final whistle,” concluded the Inter coach.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1317. Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Rachel Fieldhouse is a reporter for Nature in Sydney, Australia.

Many giant viruses can be seen under a light microscope.Credit: Gabrielle Voinot/Eurelios/Look at Sciences/SPL

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying previously unknown giant viruses inside their guts. Microbiologists say that these ‘egoviruses’ could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly. The findings are published in Nature1.

Large and giant viruses in the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are a vast group of DNA viruses — some are so big that they can be seen under a light microscope — that mostly infect single-celled organisms in the environment.

Poxviruses are an outlier in the giant-virus world because they can directly infect humans and animals and their origin is a mystery, says Fasséli Coulibaly, a structural biologist at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia. Egoviruses could be the evolutionary bridge between microorganism-infecting giant viruses called asfuviruses and pathogenic poxviruses, he says.

Tom Delmont, a microbial ecologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research in Paris, and his colleagues discovered egoviruses while combing through online libraries of metagenomes. These contain the genetic information of all the organisms in a particular environment, which means that researchers can hunt for microbes without having to cultivate them. When the team scanned for a single gene found in most nucleocytoviruses, they discovered egoviruses — the only type of nucleocytovirus that is prevalent in the gut.

They found egovirus DNA in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people. One of these clades is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the global population, on the basis of the presence of at least one of two egovirus proteins in the samples they analysed.

The researchers detected these proteins in samples spanning a large proportion of the human population, from the Hadza, a hunter-gatherer group in Tanzania, to populations in Europe, the United States and South America, says Delmont. That suggests that egoviruses have been inhabiting the human gut for a long time, he adds.

That egoviruses are found in many animal species, including people, and are widespread around the world shows that giant viruses are more diverse than previously thought, says Subir Sarker, a molecular virologist at James Cook University in Townsville, Queensland. “This is a really groundbreaking study,” he adds.

To identify potential hosts for egoviruses in the gut, the team compared the amount of genetic overlap between egoviruses and organisms with a nucleus. The researchers found the most overlap with single-celled organisms that help ruminants, such as cows, to digest their food.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03766-w

#1316. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1312. Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

The 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

#1309. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

Listening to Carrick repeatedly talking about the need for humility, hard work, pride, sacrifice and resilience was a reminder of how the values that were once taken for granted at this football club have steadily been eroded.

Wayne Rooney said this week that United’s players were “selfish” and “babies”. Many top players over the years have been selfish but it helped drive them and, in turn, their team to great heights, but the same cannot be said about the current bunch.

It feels at times as if it can be a long way away but it doesn’t take too much to flip the other way and we’re more than capable of doing that, I totally believe that.

We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

Carrick had clearly thought hard about how he was going to tackle that today and what message he wanted to get across. By name checking the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Matt Busby he was speaking about the people who exemplified the values United are all about

The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years.

I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.

No definitive answer from Carrick, who says he wants to do what is best for the football club.

There ends the broadcast section of the press conference after about 15 minutes.

My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

Principles are so important. We can win games, lose games, hopefully not but it can happen.

He says loads of conversations have been going on. He says it’s his responsibility “to lead” and that “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and keep everyone else dry.”

Carrick adds on the Fernandes burglary. “It’s an awful thing to go through and we’re doing a lot of things to support him and his family.”

It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United.

Wayne Rooney is top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.

Sir Alex Ferguson is the best manager of all-time. The greatest, for me. And working for him, his main priority was Manchester United.

Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.

We’ve lost our way if I’m totally honest but we’ll get back what it takes.

Carrick has come in, trailed by the Amazon cameras, sat down and made an address for five minutes before taking any questions. Hopefully he will be in position by half-past, but it is not unlike managers to keep everyone waiting.

My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my “strong personality”. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.

Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact.

A number of factors may be to blame: recruitment errors, paralysing pressure and a bad dressing-room culture among them. It is time to get back to basics.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

#1305. Jutglà and Swedberg doubles send Celta Vigo through 5-0 at ten-man Salamanca

Celta Vigo were rarely troubled in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Friday 13 November. Jutglà struck twice before the half-hour mark, and Swedberg added a late double after Salamanca UDS had gone down to ten men.

The Galician side were 3-0 up at the break at Villares de la Reina. They finished with goals from three different players and assists from five team-mates, against a Salamanca side coached by Jorge García.

Jutglà opened the scoring in the 15th minute, converting an assist from Milla. Eight minutes later he struck again, this time set up by Febas, to put Celta firmly in control.

Antañón made it three in the 39th minute from an Arcos assist. The tie was effectively settled before the interval.

Salamanca’s evening grew harder after the restart. Murua was booked in the 54th minute, and Levrand was shown a straight red card in the 61st minute, leaving the hosts a man short for the final half-hour.

Celta’s only caution came when Lago was booked in the 72nd minute. The visitors then took advantage of the extra man late on. Swedberg scored in the 80th minute from an Aspas assist and struck again in the 82nd, with Galán providing the pass.

Opara was also booked for Salamanca in the 89th minute as the hosts saw out the closing stages.

The result echoes the previous meeting between the clubs in this competition. Celta won 7-0 in Salamanca on 3 December 2024.

5 goles para selar o pase á seguinte rolda 🔥#UDSCelta ⋄ #CopaDelRey pic.twitter.com/v5Kqou8U4w

The win is Celta’s first in any competition since their 2-1 victory over Celtic. In between, they drew 0-0 with Real Betis, lost 3-0 to Rayo Vallecano and 2-1 to Union St. Gilloise, and drew 0-0 with Levante.

For Salamanca, the defeat ended a winning run in which they had beaten Gimnástica Segoviana 1-0 and Real Ávila 3-1.

Salamanca return to Segunda División RFEF Group 5 action at home to Albacete II on Wednesday 18 November. Celta face a far tougher assignment in LaLiga, travelling to Real Madrid on Saturday 21 November.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1301. Baena and Pubill keep Spain perfect as ten-man Czechia are beaten 2-0 in Prague

Spain won 2-0 in Prague despite missing Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal, with Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena converting a penalty and Marc Pubill adding a late second. The win keeps the world champions perfect in Nations League Group A3 and leaves them needing only a draw against England on Sunday.

Spain beat ten-man Czechia 2-0 at the Letná Stadium in Prague on Thursday. They did it without three of their leading names. Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Mikel Oyarzabal were all missing. Atlético Madrid’s Álex Baena struck from the spot, and Marc Pubill added a late second. The world champions remain perfect in Group A3 before Sunday’s decider against England.

Conditions were raw. The game was played in 4°C, with light drizzle and humidity above 90%, the Spanish federation said. Czechia are coached by the Spaniard Santi Denia.

Chances were scarce before the break. Dean Huijsen’s header was Spain’s only open-play effort on target in the first half, and it was easily saved. The breakthrough came from the penalty spot. Lukáš Ambros was penalised for handball in the area. Baena’s powerful penalty beat goalkeeper Matěj Kovář.

Spain thought they had doubled the lead after half-time. VAR ruled out an effort by Yéremy Pino. The game was physical. Referee Nikola Dabanovic booked Pedro Porro in the 12th minute and Mikel Merino in the 69th. He then dismissed Krejčí, leaving the hosts a man down for the closing stages.

Spain made the extra man count deep into added time. Pubill won the ball back in Czechia’s half and rolled it into the bottom corner. That settled the contest. For Atlético followers, Baena’s goal was the night’s highlight. Fermín López, by contrast, is still waiting for his first Spain goal.

The victory was Spain’s 12th in a row and their fifth straight win in the Nations League. ESPN said it stretched their record unbeaten run in all competitions. Spain’s last defeat came against Colombia in March 2024. Czechia, meanwhile, have lost every Nations League game this season.

England kept pace on the same night. They beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley and sit three points behind Spain. That sets up a straight shoot-out for first place. A draw against England at the Metropolitano on Sunday will be enough for Spain to finish first in the group.

#1299. Atlético Madrid buy 50% of Atlético FC, Guayaquil’s newly promoted Serie B champions

Atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season. The deal gives the Spanish club its first affiliate in South America before the Ecuadorian team steps up to Serie A in 2027.

The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.

The move had been signalled earlier in the year. On Friday 20 February 2026, Atlético said it would share sporting, institutional and commercial expertise with Atlético FC and might take a stake in the following months, El Comercio reported.

Regarded as Ecuador’s largest non-profit organisation, the Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil operates in all 24 of the country’s provinces.

The club’s route into Serie B was unusual. It took over the place of Atlético Vinotinto, which could not use it because its affiliate Vinotinto FC had been relegated. The team also changed its name from Atlético JBG to Atlético FC.

Promotion came on 15 October 2026 with a 1-0 win over Independiente Juniors. Fidel Martínez scored the goal. A week later, on Thursday 22 October, a 2-2 draw against Cuenca Juniors at the Estadio Alejandro Serrano sealed the title. That match was the ninth round of the promotion hexagonal.

Across the campaign the side scored 39 goals and conceded 21. It became the 37th different club to win Ecuador’s Serie B. The team is coached by Carlos Santamarina, who comes from Atlético’s academy.

The promotion also reshapes the city’s football map. Guayaquil will have four clubs in the 2027 Serie A: Atlético FC, Barcelona SC, Emelec and Guayaquil City.

Mexico and Canada already host clubs in the Madrid side’s network of linked teams, through Atlético de San Luis and Atlético Ottawa.

The investment builds on years of groundwork in Ecuador. Atlético and the Junta signed their original strategic agreement on Monday 24 July 2023 at the charity’s sports complex. Under that deal, the club’s academy would apply its coaching model to the Junta’s football division. At the time, that division served 2,500 children from vulnerable backgrounds.

In June 2026 the club put the number of young players at more than 14,000. That same month, chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín visited the academy’s Guayaquil base. With the Junta’s delegation, he watched an Atlético FC match and greeted Santamarina.

El Atlético Fútbol Club se une a la familia rojiblanca.

Nuestro club hace efectiva la adquisición del 50% del equipo ecuatoriano, que logró el ascenso a la Serie A en octubre de la mano del técnico de la Academia Carlos Santamarina.

— Atlético de Madrid (@Atleti) November 13, 2026

For Atlético, the stake creates a direct link between that youth work and a senior professional team.

The board holds its first meeting next week. It will elect a president proposed by Atlético and appoint a general manager.

#1297. Tebas lists Real Madrid’s attacks on LaLiga a month after club demanded his resignation

LaLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas says Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez said Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

Tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

The thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club said Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas said the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

The dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Tomás González-Martín sostiene en El Debate que un presidente de LaLiga no puede dedicarse a atacar a uno de sus socios. Para sostener su argumento, omite una parte esencial: las acusaciones que Florentino Pérez y los canales oficiales del Real Madrid…

— Javier Tebas Medrano (@Tebasjavier) November 15, 2026

Pérez now faces his members. Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. The only item at the extraordinary assembly is a proposal to ratify tennis player Rafael Nadal as a board member. The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.
